nodes.label: command priority
nodes.def: A metadata field indicating the urgency or precedence level of a command message, used by schedulers and routers to order or filter command processing.

nodes.label: command target
nodes.def: The logical or physical destination endpoint to which a command message is addressed, specifying which receiver should process the invocation.

nodes.label: command timeout
nodes.def: The maximum duration a sender will wait for a command to complete before considering it failed; exceeding this triggers timeout handling or retry.

nodes.label: composed message processor
nodes.def: A processor that splits an incoming composite message, routes each part through separate paths, then aggregates the results.

nodes.label: content enricher
nodes.def: A transformer that supplements an incoming message with additional data fetched from an external source before forwarding.

nodes.label: correlation identifier
nodes.def: A unique ID placed on both request and reply messages so the sender can match responses to their originating calls.

nodes.label: cp poison message
nodes.def: A message that has caused repeated processing failures or is structurally unprocessable and blocks channel progress if retained.

nodes.label: cp purge history
nodes.def: An audit log recording which messages were purged, when, under which policy, and the channel_state_snapshot at purge time for replay and tuning.

nodes.label: cp purge policy
nodes.def: A set of rules defining which messages qualify for purging: age threshold, retry exhaustion, poison detection criteria, or pattern matching on content.

nodes.label: cp purge scheduler
nodes.def: The component that periodically evaluates threshold_condition and, when true, dispatches purge_action against the target channel.

nodes.label: cp purge trigger
nodes.def: A condition that initiates a channel purge cycle; may be time-based, count-based, or event-based such as threshold_exceeded.

nodes.label: cp stale message
nodes.def: A message that has exceeded its relevance window or idle duration and no longer carries actionable data for downstream consumers.

nodes.label: dm 007
nodes.def: document_origin: Metadata identifying the originating system, agent, or process that produced the document_message.

nodes.label: dm 009
nodes.def: schema_registry_entry: An entry in the message_type_registry binding a business_object_type to its document_schema and authorized handlers.

nodes.label: end to end acknowledge
nodes.def: A correlation pattern where the final consumer sends an acknowledgment that propagates back through the routing chain to the original sender.

nodes.label: envelope wrapper
nodes.def: A transformer that wraps or unwraps a message in an envelope to add or strip protocol-level headers for transport.

nodes.label: event driven architecture
nodes.def: An architectural style where system components react to events published to a message bus rather than being invoked directly.

nodes.label: event subscription
nodes.def: The registration of a consumer's interest in receiving messages from a particular channel or topic based on content or type.

nodes.label: exactly once delivery
nodes.def: Message delivery semantics ensuring that a message is processed precisely one time, combining delivery guarantees with deduplication.

nodes.label: fault payload
nodes.def: A data envelope containing error details returned when an operation fails, typically including fault code, description, and optional context for recovery.

nodes.label: health check endpoint
nodes.def: A monitoring interface that exposes integration component status (channels healthy, queues depth, processing lag) for observability.

nodes.label: invalid message channel
nodes.def: A channel that captures malformed or unprocessable messages for manual inspection instead of blocking the main flow.

nodes.label: message datatype
nodes.def: The classification or schema identifier of a message that determines which datatype channels it can traverse.

nodes.label: message expiration
nodes.def: A property on a message indicating it becomes invalid after a certain time and should be discarded if not delivered.

nodes.label: messaging gateway
nodes.def: A Façade that exposes integration functionality to internal clients while hiding the underlying messaging API and complexity.

nodes.label: messaging translator
nodes.def: A bridge component that converts between the enterprise's canonical data model and the external system's proprietary format.

nodes.label: point to point channel
nodes.def: A channel with exactly one consumer per message; guarantees that exactly one receiver processes each message.

nodes.label: process manager
nodes.def: A stateful component that orchestrates a multi-step business process by sending messages to channels and handling responses.

nodes.label: recipient list
nodes.def: A router that sends the same message to a list of recipients computed at runtime from the message content or context.

nodes.label: remote procedure invocation
nodes.def: Integration where one system exposes a callable API and another synchronously invokes it as if it were local.

nodes.label: resequencer
nodes.def: A router that reorders a stream of messages into the correct sequence before passing them downstream.

nodes.label: result payload
nodes.def: A data envelope containing the return value or outcome produced by a successfully executed operation, structured to match the expected response schema.

nodes.label: return address
nodes.def: Metadata on a reply message indicating which channel and possibly which queue the response should be routed to.

nodes.label: scatter gather
nodes.def: A router that broadcasts a request to multiple recipients and then collects and consolidates all their responses.

nodes.label: transactional integration
nodes.def: Integration that groups message production or consumption with local database updates into a single atomic unit of work.

nodes.label: type matching check
nodes.def: The validation that a message's actual type matches a datatype channel's declared type at the point of send or receive.

nodes.label: type schema binding
nodes.def: The linkage between a datatype channel and the formal schema or structure definition of its accepted message type.

nodes.label: untyped channel
nodes.def: A channel without a declared datatype that accepts messages of any type, serving as the contrast to datatype channels.

nodes.label: asynchronous messaging
nodes.def: Messaging semantics where the sender does not block waiting for the receiver to process the message before continuing.

nodes.label: at least once delivery
nodes.def: Message delivery semantics where a message is retried until acknowledged, guaranteeing delivery but allowing possible duplicates.

nodes.label: at most once delivery
nodes.def: Message delivery semantics where a message may be lost but is never redelivered; sender does not retry on failure.

nodes.label: attachment
nodes.def: Secondary data elements or files appended to the document message beyond its primary business payload.

nodes.label: canonical form
nodes.def: The normalized or standardized representation of the document after transformation, serving as the canonical data format.

nodes.label: channel bridge
nodes.def: A connection point that joins two channel segments or a channel to an external system, enabling message flow across the boundary while preserving channel semantics.

nodes.label: channel purger
nodes.def: A system management pattern that periodically clears a channel of stale or poison messages to reset system state.

nodes.label: channel type declaration
nodes.def: The explicit binding of a message datatype to a channel at channel creation or configuration time, establishing the type contract.

nodes.label: channel typing discipline
nodes.def: The classification of datatype channels by typing rigor: static typing enforces type at compile/build time, dynamic typing enforces at message inspection time.

nodes.label: choreography
nodes.def: A decentralized integration style where each system knows only its own part of the process; there is no central orchestrator.

nodes.label: cmd 001
nodes.def: operation_identifier — the name or qualified identifier of the operation being invoked on the receiver

nodes.label: cmd 002
nodes.def: operation_arguments — structured data representing the parameters passed to the invoked operation

nodes.label: cmd 003
nodes.def: command_target — the destination endpoint service or receiver on which the operation is to be executed

nodes.label: cmd 004
nodes.def: command_priority — urgency level that influences routing queue ordering and processor scheduling

nodes.label: cmd 005
nodes.def: idempotency_key — unique value the receiver uses to detect and suppress duplicate command executions

nodes.label: cmd 006
nodes.def: command_timeout — duration after which the sender abandons waiting for execution result

nodes.label: cmd 007
nodes.def: target_interface_version — version identifier enabling the receiver to select the correct operation contract

nodes.label: cmd 008
nodes.def: execution_context — metadata about the calling environment such as principal identity and correlation scope

nodes.label: cmd 009
nodes.def: result_payload — data returned by successful command execution part of request_reply exchange

nodes.label: cmd 010
nodes.def: fault_payload — structured error information returned when command execution fails part of request_reply

nodes.label: content filter
nodes.def: A transformer that removes unwanted fields from a message, reducing payload size or stripping sensitive data.

nodes.label: content integrity
nodes.def: A cryptographic checksum or hash value computed over the document content to detect unauthorized alterations in transit.

nodes.label: content router for documents
nodes.def: The application of content_based_router to a document_message using payload fields to determine routing destination.

nodes.label: cp channel state snapshot
nodes.def: A point-in-time capture of channel metrics (depth, oldest_message_age, error_rate) used to evaluate purge_policy conditions before triggering a purge.

nodes.label: cp retention window
nodes.def: A configurable time interval after which messages become stale_message candidates for purging; part of purge_policy definition.

nodes.label: delayer
nodes.def: A router that holds messages for a configurable duration before forwarding them, implementing delayed delivery semantics.

nodes.label: detour
nodes.def: A system management pattern that reroutes messages through a debugging or inspection step before resuming normal delivery.

nodes.label: dm 006
nodes.def: processing_hint: An optional non-directive annotation suggesting preferred handling, urgency, or routing preference without constituting a command.

nodes.label: dm 008
nodes.def: payload_extractor: A component that retrieves specific fields from the payload_structure for routing, correlation, or downstream transformation.

nodes.label: doc payload
nodes.def: The complete data content carried by a document_message, representing the full information payload without prescribing receiver action.

nodes.label: document classifier
nodes.def: A component or rule set that examines document content to determine its payload type category for downstream routing.

nodes.label: document content
nodes.def: The actual business data carried by the document message, constituting the primary payload that the receiver processes.

nodes.label: document distinguishes from command
nodes.def: document_message differs from command_message by carrying data rather than prescribing method invocations.

nodes.label: document semantic type
nodes.def: The domain-specific classification of a document_message payload, distinguishing purchase orders from invoices or other business documents.

nodes.label: durable subscriber
nodes.def: A subscriber registration that survives broker restarts; undelivered messages are queued and delivered once the subscriber reconnects.

nodes.label: dynamic router
nodes.def: A router that consults a registry or lookup table at runtime to determine destinations, allowing routing rules to change without redeployment.

nodes.label: enterprise service bus
nodes.def: An architectural platform that combines messaging, routing, transformation, and protocol bridging into a single integration middleware layer.

nodes.label: execution context
nodes.def: A structured record of runtime state passed alongside a command, providing the environment information needed to correctly process the operation invocation.

nodes.label: file transfer integration
nodes.def: Integration via shared filesystem where each system produces/consumes files, requiring conventions on naming and polling.

nodes.label: idempotency key
nodes.def: A unique identifier assigned to a command that allows receivers to detect and discard duplicate submissions, ensuring safe retries without double execution.

nodes.label: list of interceptors
nodes.def: A system management pattern that registers interceptor objects to run before or after message processing for cross-cutting concerns.

nodes.label: load balancer
nodes.def: A router that distributes messages across multiple equivalent receiver instances to spread processing load.

nodes.label: message filter
nodes.def: A router that discards messages that do not meet a predicate condition, suppressing unwanted messages from downstream consumers.

nodes.label: operation arguments
nodes.def: The parameter values supplied to the operation being invoked by a command message, structured according to the target interface's argument schema.

nodes.label: commit object
nodes.def: Type-3 git object containing tree SHA, parent SHA(s), author, committer, timestamp, and message; forms the history DAG backbone.

nodes.label: tree entry mode
nodes.def: Octal mode in tree object: 100644 (regular file), 100755 (executable), 040000 (subtree), 120000 (symlink), 160000 (submodule).

nodes.label: tree object
nodes.def: Type-2 git object listing directory entries as (mode, name, sha1) tuples; represents a single directory snapshot at a point in time.

nodes.label: ref pointer
nodes.def: Named file under .git/refs/ containing a SHA-1; represents a branch tip, tag, or remote-tracking branch; updated atomically during operations.

nodes.label: blob object
nodes.def: Type-1 git object storing raw file contents verbatim; identified by SHA-1 of content; no filename or metadata retained.

nodes.label: sha1 hash
nodes.def: 160-bit cryptographic hash computed over object content; serves as object's unique addressable name in git's content-addressable store.

nodes.label: delta compression
nodes.def: Git's storage optimization encoding an object as a series of copy/insert commands relative to a base object; OFS_DELTA uses relative offsets; REF_DELTA uses absolute SHA-1.

nodes.label: object database
nodes.def: Directory-backed key-value store under .git/objects/; loose objects stored as zlib-deflated files keyed by SHA-1; packed objects aggregated into packfiles.

nodes.label: reachability
nodes.def: Property of an object being transitively accessible from another; defines ancestry in the commit DAG; basis for gc, merge-base, and history queries.

nodes.label: author field
nodes.def: Name and email in commit object identifying primary creator; distinct from committer who applied the patch.

nodes.label: commit graph
nodes.def: Binary file .git/objects/info/commit-graph storing commit reachability, generation numbers, and bloom filter data off the critical path.

nodes.label: mode type bits
nodes.def: The upper bits of the octal mode identifying the entry's object category: regular file, directory, symlink, or submodule; encoded in the first two octal digits.

nodes.label: object type inspection
nodes.def: git cat-file -t reveals object type; git cat-file -s shows byte size; git cat-file -p pretty-prints content; git rev-list walks commit graph.

nodes.label: commit message encoding encoding value
nodes.def: The character encoding name stored in the encoding header (UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, etc.); controls byte-to-character interpretation of the message bytes.

nodes.label: commit message encoding transcoding logic
nodes.def: git's internal conversion from the stored encoding_value to the requested log_encoding_flag encoding; uses iconv-style conversion with loss handling.

nodes.label: packfile
nodes.def: Single binary file consolidating many objects via delta compression; named pack-*.pack with companion .idx index; vastly reduces repository size.

nodes.label: submodule pointer
nodes.def: Entry in a parent repository's tree object referencing a specific commit of a nested repository; stored as mode 160000 with commit SHA-1.

nodes.label: maintenance task
nodes.def: git maintenance subcommand scheduling background optimization: gc, commit-graph rebuild, incremental-repack, prefetch, prune.

nodes.label: partial clone
nodes.def: Clone with --filter omitting blob objects from transfer; missing blobs retrieved on demand via fetch-object; enables huge-repository workflows.

nodes.label: tag object
nodes.def: Type-4 git object wrapping another object with a tag name, tagger info, and message; typically used for annotated release markers.

nodes.label: author timestamp
nodes.def: Integer Unix timestamp recording when the author created the change; represents seconds since epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC) in the author field.

nodes.label: commit message encoding encoding header
nodes.def: Optional header line 'encoding <encoding-name>' in a commit object's raw text; git stores whatever the user wrote verbatim.

nodes.label: content addressable store
nodes.def: Property that object identity derives solely from its content hash; same content always yields identical identifier regardless of path or history.

nodes.label: head pointer
nodes.def: Symbolic ref .git/HEAD pointing to current branch name or directly to a SHA-1 in detached mode; moves on checkout.

nodes.label: index file
nodes.def: Binary staging area at .git/index listing path->blob SHA-1 mappings plus stage numbers for unmerged entries; fast diff vs tree computation.

nodes.label: merkle tree property
nodes.def: 拜占庭容错特性: tree SHA derived from entry hashes and names; any content change ripples upward; enables tamper-evident history without full content comparison.

nodes.label: packfile index
nodes.def: Binary lookup table (.idx) enabling O(log n) SHA-1 to offset resolution within a packfile; also stores CRC-32 for integrity verification.

nodes.label: parent commit list
nodes.def: Comma-separated list of parent SHA-1s in commit object; first parent first enables linear history heuristics; octopush uses multi-parent.

nodes.label: ref backend
nodes.def: Virtual filesystem layer for ref storage; files backend for loose refs, reftable backend for high-scale; configured via extensions.refStorage.

nodes.label: reflog
nodes.def: Append-only log at .git/logs/ tracking all ref changes with old SHA, new SHA, timestamp, and actor; enables recovery from accidental resets or branch deletions.

nodes.label: unreachable object
nodes.def: Object with valid content but no reference path from any ref, reflog entry, or other reachable object; candidate for garbage collection.

nodes.label: alternates object db
nodes.def: File .git/objects/info/alternates listing paths to shared object stores; enables disk-space savings across clones.

nodes.label: author date
nodes.def: Composite of author_timestamp and author_timezone; git log --date= formats this value.

nodes.label: author name
nodes.def: String component of the author field in a commit object specifying the primary creator's display name; appears before the email in the standard <name> <email> format.

nodes.label: bundle format
nodes.def: Self-contained .git-bundle file encoding ref updates and reachable objects; enables offline transfer via removable media.

nodes.label: clean filter
nodes.def: Configured program git attributes runs on git checkout; transforms blob from object store before writing to working tree.

nodes.label: commit graph write
nodes.def: git commit-graph write traverses reachable commits and writes binary graph; --split merges small chains; --append adds commits to existing graph.

nodes.label: commit message encoding message bytes
nodes.def: Raw byte sequence forming the commit message body; decoded using encoding_value (or assumed UTF-8) to produce display characters.

nodes.label: commit message encoding transcoded message
nodes.def: The output of transcoding_logic: message_bytes decoded then re-encoded into log_encoding_flag; git log emits this to the terminal.

nodes.label: committer field
nodes.def: Name, email, timestamp, and timezone offset in commit object; records who committed (not necessarily who authored).

nodes.label: custom object db
nodes.def: Alternative backend via GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY or extensions.objectFormat; allows SHA-256, shared storage, or plugin-based stores.

nodes.label: executable file mode
nodes.def: Mode 100755; regular file with execute bits set; Git marks it this way to preserve the executable bit across platforms that handle it differently.

nodes.label: fetch head
nodes.def: Temporary .git/FETCH_HEAD file recording all branches fetched and their merge configuration for the next pull operation.

nodes.label: fsck integrity
nodes.def: git fsck traverses all reachable objects validating SHA-1 linkage, ref integrity, and accessibility; reports dangling and unreachable.

nodes.label: gc prune
nodes.def: Garbage collection process expunging unreachable objects older than prune.window; configurable via gc.prune expire and git prune.

nodes.label: graft point
nodes.def: File .git/info/grafts (or .git/shallow) overriding or truncating commit ancestry; used for repository imports with incomplete history.

nodes.label: hash object write
nodes.def: Flag hash --write causes git to store the computed object in .git/objects/ after hashing; idempotent on repeat.

nodes.label: heads namespace
nodes.def: Namespace .git/refs/heads/ containing local branch references; each file = branch name; its SHA-1 = tip commit.

nodes.label: mode bit format
nodes.def: Base-8 positional numeral system used to encode file mode; Git stores exactly 6 octal digits representing 18 bits of mode information.

nodes.label: octopus merge
nodes.def: Merge commit with more than two parents; octopus strategy combines multiple branches; refs/heads/main lists all parents in merge commit object.

nodes.label: packed refs
nodes.def: Consolidated .git/packed-refs file containing refs not in loose format; created by git pack-refs; enables faster startup on repos with many refs.

nodes.label: packfile bitmap
nodes.def: Reachability bitmap at packfile end enabling fast network transfer negotiation and clone/fetch optimization by marking all reachable objects.

nodes.label: packfile negotiation
nodes.def: Smart protocol phase where server advertises reachable refs and client computes minimum packfile of missing objects using haves/wants.

nodes.label: rebase replay
nodes.def: Replay commits as new objects onto new base; each original commit replaced; original SHA-1s abandoned; creates new history branch.

nodes.label: refspec
nodes.def: Pattern mapping source to destination ref during fetch/push: [+]<src>:<dst>; enables selective branch transfer and namespace rewriting.

nodes.label: regular file mode
nodes.def: Mode 100644; standard blob-backed file with read permission for all and write for owner; the default for non-executable files committed to Git.

nodes.label: remotes namespace
nodes.def: Namespace .git/refs/remotes/ containing remote-tracking branches; updated by fetch, not by user edits; represent server state.

nodes.label: replace ref
nodes.def: Reference under refs/replace/ mapping an object SHA to a substitute SHA; transparent to most commands; allows history rewriting without modifying history.

nodes.label: sha1 collision resistance
nodes.def: Property that finding two distinct contents with same SHA-1 requires ~2^80 operations; git relies on this for object identity.

nodes.label: sha256 migration
nodes.def: Gradual transition from SHA-1 to SHA-256 object names; support for SHA-256-only repositories since git 2.29; object format stored in config.

nodes.label: shallow clone
nodes.def: Clone with .git/shallow cut-off file listing shallow commit SHAs; prevents fetching ancestors beyond the boundary.

nodes.label: smudge filter
nodes.def: Configured program git attributes runs on git add; transforms working-tree file before storing as object; lazy loading via .gitattributes.

nodes.label: stash ref
nodes.def: Pseudo-branch at refs/stash maintained by git stash; each stash entry is a commit whose tree captures working-directory state.

nodes.label: subtree mode
nodes.def: Mode 040000; entry points to a nested tree object representing a directory; the tree entry name contains a forward slash but the slash is not stored in the entry itself.

nodes.label: symlink mode
nodes.def: Mode 120000; entry points to a blob object containing the target path as raw bytes; the blob content is the symlink destination, not the link data itself.

nodes.label: tree entry name
nodes.def: Null-terminated byte string within tree entry; may contain slash for subdirectory entries; case-sensitive on all platforms.

nodes.label: worktree pointer
nodes.def: File .git/worktrees/<name>/HEAD and GITDIR files linking a linked working tree to the main repository's object store and refs.

nodes.label: zlib compression
nodes.def: Deflate compression applied to all loose object content and packfile entries; balance of speed and ratio; configurable per object type via core.compression.

nodes.label: annotated tag signature
nodes.def: PGP signature stored within tag object body; verified by git tag -v; authenticates the tagged object SHA-1.

nodes.label: author email
nodes.def: String component of the author field in a commit object specifying the primary creator's email address; appears in angle brackets after the name in the standard <name> <email> form

nodes.label: author ident
nodes.def: Full author identity string in the form 'Name <email> timestamp timezone_offset' embedded in a commit object's author header; the canonical representation of author_field.

nodes.label: author identification
nodes.def: The combination of author_name and author_email forming the author's identity within the commit object.

nodes.label: author rfc2822
nodes.def: The RFC 2822 formatted author line: "author <name> <email> <timestamp> <timezone>" stored in commit object body.

nodes.label: author timezone
nodes.def: String timezone offset in the author field following the timestamp; formatted as +HHMM or -HHMM indicating hours and minutes east or west of UTC.

nodes.label: author vs committer
nodes.def: The semantic distinction: author created the patch content; committer applied it to the repository; git blame uses author_field as the primary attribution.

nodes.label: bisect log
nodes.def: refs/bisect/* pseudo-refs tracking midpoints and test results during git bisect; --no-checkout mode walks history without checkout.

nodes.label: blob prefetch
nodes.def: Git fetch-object or protocol v2 advertisements retrieving missing blob content on demand from partial clone; requires server support.

nodes.label: blob split threshold
nodes.def: Configuration core.bigFileThreshold beyond which git may store deltas instead of full content in packfiles.

nodes.label: bloom filter index
nodes.def: Commit-graph embedded data structure encoding paths modified per commit; powers git log --S <string> --throughput optimization.

nodes.label: branch tracking assignment
nodes.def: Remote-tracking ref establishing upstream relationship; configured via branch.<name>.remote and branch.<name>.merge; used for push.default and @{upstream}.

nodes.label: byte string content
nodes.def: The raw byte sequence forming the name; git stores no encoding assumption, no null bytes permitted within the name itself, and no guaranteed UTF-8 validity.

nodes.label: case preservation property
nodes.def: The name bytes are stored verbatim and compared byte-for-byte, making the entry case-sensitive on all operating systems including case-insensitive filesystems where the working tre

nodes.label: cherry pick delta
nodes.def: Apply single commit's diff as new commit; preserves original author; generates new SHA-1; records original SHA-1 in commit message.

nodes.label: commit date ordering
nodes.def: Revision list ordering by commit timestamp; --date-order flag; faster than topological but produces non-ancestor-first sequences.

nodes.label: commit filter
nodes.def: Revision traversal predicate (--since, --author, --grep, --S, --G) restricting which commits appear in output.

nodes.label: commit graph verify
nodes.def: git commit-graph verify reads graph and validates generation numbers, checksum, and fanout structure; reports corruption.

nodes.label: commit message encoding
nodes.def: Commit object may record encoding header; git log --encoding=UTF-8 transcodes as needed; enables non-ASCII commit messages.

nodes.label: commit message encoding display encoding
nodes.def: The terminal or output stream encoding git uses when writing the transcoded_message; git assumes UTF-8 output if terminal encoding is unset.

nodes.label: commit message encoding encoding absence
nodes.def: State when a commit object lacks an encoding header; git treats the message as UTF-8 by default per the unicode interpretation rule.

nodes.label: commit message encoding encoding fallback
nodes.def: Fallback behavior when transcoding_logic cannot map a character; typically replaces with a substitution character or skips the byte.

nodes.label: commit message encoding log encoding flag
nodes.def: git log flag --encoding=<enc> specifying the target encoding for transcoded output; overrides the stored encoding for display purposes.

nodes.label: commit message encoding original encoding
nodes.def: Alias for encoding_value; the encoding recorded at commit time distinguishing the message's original byte interpretation from the display encoding.

nodes.label: committer ident
nodes.def: Full committer identity string in form 'Name <email> timestamp timezone_offset' in the commit object; distinct from author_ident.

nodes.label: compression level
nodes.def: Integer -1 (zlib default), 0 (store), 1-9 (fast to best); set via core.compression or per-object pack-objects --compression.

nodes.label: copy instruction
nodes.def: Packfile command copying bytes from base object at offset+length; encodes file copy without recompression.

nodes.label: crc32 checksum
nodes.def: Checksum stored per object in packfile index; verified on read to detect corruption before decompression.

nodes.label: dangling blob
nodes.def: Blob object with no parent tree entry; arises from aborted rebase or staged-but-uncommitted content; harmless but obscures analysis.

nodes.label: delta island
nodes.def: Packfile grouping mechanism isolating objects reachable via specific refs; prevents cross-island delta sharing; aids monorepo incremental fetch.

nodes.label: embedded null rejection
nodes.def: The rule that a tree entry name cannot contain an internal null byte because null is the field terminator; any such byte would truncate the name prematurely.

nodes.label: empty tree sha
nodes.def: SHA-1 of the empty tree (tree with zero entries): 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904; used as synthetic parent of root commits.

nodes.label: forward slash byte
nodes.def: The octet value 0x2F representing the ASCII forward slash character; signals subdirectory boundary in tree entry name byte sequences.

nodes.label: fsync object write
nodes.def: System call flushing object file to durable storage; controlled by core.fsyncObjectFiles; trades safety against write throughput.

nodes.label: generation number
nodes.def: Integer in commit-graph measuring topological distance from roots; enables fast ancestor queries without traversing full commit history.

nodes.label: graph tip
nodes.def: Commit referenced by a branch tip; all ancestors reachable; descendant commits unreferenced subject to gc if no other path retains them.

nodes.label: hook environment
nodes.def: Environment variables (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH) passed to hook executables; quarantine prevents bad objects from entering repo.

nodes.label: hook trigger
nodes.def: Executable script under .git/hooks/ invoked by specific git commands (pre-commit, post-commit, pre-rebase, etc.); nonzero exit aborts operation.

nodes.label: insert instruction
nodes.def: Packfile command appending literal byte sequence to output; the raw new content not derivable from base.

nodes.label: linear history heuristic
nodes.def: Git's default rebase behavior assumes first parent path is mainline; git log --first-parent exposes linearized view; bisect follows first parent.

nodes.label: loose object
nodes.def: Individual compressed file stored at .git/objects/xx/xxxx...; fast to write but inefficient at scale; one object per file.

nodes.label: maintenance scheduler
nodes.def: Background git maintenance --scheduled running via cron or systemd timer; config thresholds in maintenance.<task>.schedule.

nodes.label: mode permission bits
nodes.def: The lower 9 bits (three octal digits) encoding Unix owner/group/other read-write-execute permissions; displayed as the last three digits of the 6-digit octal mode.

nodes.label: mode zero padding
nodes.def: The leading zero in modes like 100644 and 040000 ensures consistent 6-digit width; the zero fills the third octal digit reserved for special file type flags.

nodes.label: multi pack index
nodes.def: Compound .midx file spanning multiple packfiles; enables cross-pack object queries and accelerates repack scenarios.

nodes.label: note object
nodes.def: Blob-like object linked via refs/notes/commits/ to commits; provides annotation layer outside normal commit history.

nodes.label: null termination semantics
nodes.def: The rule that a null byte (0x00) terminates the tree entry name field, separating it from the following mode and SHA-1 blob reference within the tree entry binary structure.

nodes.label: object header
nodes.def: Four-byte prefix of every loose object: type byte + space + decimal size + null byte before payload; enables streaming deserialization.

nodes.label: octopus strategy
nodes.def: Merge strategy handling 3+ branch tips simultaneously; creates single commit with all parents; avoids intermediate pairwise merges.

nodes.label: ofs delta
nodes.def: Delta format encoding base object as relative offset within packfile; safer for streaming than REF_DELTA which names base by SHA-1.

nodes.label: ours strategy
nodes.def: Merge strategy favoring current branch content for conflicts; creates new commit with all parents but discards theirs content.

nodes.label: path separator notation

nodes.label: causal inference
nodes.def: reasoning about cause-effect relationships enabling prediction of consequences given observed causes

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.def: A reasoning task verifying that an ontology has no contradictory axioms that would eliminate all possible models.

nodes.label: counterfactual reasoning
nodes.def: reasoning about hypothetical alternative scenarios and their outcomes differing from actual observed events

nodes.label: tbox
nodes.def: The terminological box — the schema-level component of a knowledge base defining classes, properties, and their relations.

nodes.label: abox
nodes.def: The assertional box — the instance-level component of a knowledge base containing ground assertions about individuals.

nodes.label: annotation property
nodes.def: A property type for attaching metadata (labels, comments, deprecated flags) without affecting reasoning.

nodes.label: application ontology
nodes.def: A concrete ontology tailored for a specific software application, integrating and constraining reference and domain ontologies.

nodes.label: axiom
nodes.def: A logical statement in an ontology taken as fundamental truth, constraining what inferences and interpretations are valid.

nodes.label: backward chaining
nodes.def: An inference strategy starting from a query goal and recursively applying rules backwards to find supporting facts.

nodes.label: blank node
nodes.def: An anonymous resource in RDF without a stable IRI, used for existential variables or intermediate blank graph nodes.

nodes.label: cardinality restriction
nodes.def: A class restriction specifying exact, minimum, or maximum number of values a property can take for class members.

nodes.label: class
nodes.def: A concept in an ontology representing a set of entities that share common characteristics, forming the taxonomic backbone.

nodes.label: class assertion
nodes.def: statement asserting that an individual entity belongs to a specific class in the ontology classification system

nodes.label: classification
nodes.def: The process of organizing entities into classes based on shared characteristics, a core activity in ontology engineering.

nodes.label: coherence
nodes.def: The quality property of an ontology where all defined classes can have at least one instance without violating constraints.

nodes.label: concept hierarchy
nodes.def: organization of concepts in an ontology forming IS-A taxonomic relationships with superclass and subclass relations

nodes.label: concept similarity
nodes.def: metric quantifying the degree of semantic relatedness between two concepts based on shared attributes and relationships

nodes.label: confidence scoring
nodes.def: assignment of probability or confidence values to knowledge graph triples indicating reliability of each fact

nodes.label: constraint
nodes.def: A logical condition restricting valid states of a knowledge graph, violated instances indicating data quality issues.

nodes.label: constraint satisfaction
nodes.def: enforcement of logical rules and cardinality constraints ensuring knowledge graph consistency and validity

nodes.label: coreference
nodes.def: The relationship between different expressions referring to the same entity, central to entity resolution and data integration.

nodes.label: datatype property
nodes.def: A property type in OWL whose value is a literal datatype, attaching data values to entities.

nodes.label: domain ontology
nodes.def: An ontology capturing the concepts and relations specific to a particular subject area or application domain.

nodes.label: entity linking
nodes.def: process of connecting textual entity mentions to their corresponding nodes in a knowledge graph disambiguating meaning

nodes.label: evidence aggregation
nodes.def: process of combining evidence from multiple sources to determine the overall confidence in a knowledge assertion

nodes.label: forward chaining
nodes.def: An inference strategy applying rules repeatedly from premises to conclusions until no new facts can be derived.

nodes.label: graph pattern
nodes.def: A template of triple patterns with variables used in SPARQL queries to match and extract subgraphs from knowledge graphs.

nodes.label: named individual
nodes.def: An individual entity that is explicitly named with an IRI, as distinguished from anonymous blank nodes.

nodes.label: property assertion
nodes.def: triple asserting a specific relationship between two individuals or an individual and a literal value

nodes.label: qualified cardinality
nodes.def: A cardinality restriction in OWL 2 specifying the exact number of values from a specified class for a given property.

nodes.label: realization
nodes.def: The automated reasoning task of determining the most specific classes that apply to each individual in a knowledge base.

nodes.label: satisfiability
nodes.def: A reasoning task determining whether an ontology or class description can have any valid model satisfying all axioms.

nodes.label: semantic relation
nodes.def: An abstract typed connection between concepts or entities capturing meaningful domain-relevant associations.

nodes.label: subclass of
nodes.def: A taxonomic relation stating that one class is more specific than (a specialization of) another class.

nodes.label: taxonomy
nodes.def: A hierarchical classification structure organizing concepts from general to specific through subclass/superclass relationships.

nodes.label: validation
nodes.def: The checking of a knowledge graph against defined constraints to identify violations indicating errors or inconsistencies.

nodes.label: abductive reasoning
nodes.def: inference process that derives the most likely explanation for observed facts given available knowledge

nodes.label: description logic
nodes.def: The decidable fragment of first-order logic underpinning OWL, balancing expressive power with tractable reasoning.

nodes.label: disjoint class
nodes.def: ontology axiom ensuring instances of one class cannot simultaneously belong to another specified class

nodes.label: disjoint union
nodes.def: A logical axiom stating that a class is exactly the union of a collection of pairwise-disjoint classes.

nodes.label: disjoint with
nodes.def: A logical constraint stating that two classes have no common instances, enforcing mutual exclusivity in domain models.

nodes.label: distant supervision
nodes.def: weak supervision technique using knowledge graph to generate training labels for relation extraction from text

nodes.label: dl safe rule
nodes.def: A rule in OWL 2 RL/RDF that is restricted to ensure decidability and compatibility with description logic semantics.

nodes.label: domain
nodes.def: The constraint specifying which classes an entity must belong to when it appears as the subject of a given property.

nodes.label: domain range
nodes.def: constraints defining which entity types can appear as subject or object of a given property in an ontology

nodes.label: entailment
nodes.def: A logical consequence relationship where one set of statements necessarily follows from another set given the formal semantics.

nodes.label: entity
nodes.def: A real or abstract thing represented as a node in a knowledge graph, identified by a unique IRI and having properties and relationships.

nodes.label: entity disambiguation
nodes.def: process of determining which specific real-world entity a text mention refers to when multiple candidates exist

nodes.label: entity representation learning
nodes.def: learning continuous vector embeddings for entities capturing their semantic properties and graph neighborhood

nodes.label: entity resolution
nodes.def: The task of identifying when multiple entity identifiers refer to the same real-world object, also called deduplication.

nodes.label: entity typing
nodes.def: task of assigning semantic types and classes to entities determining what categories they belong to in the ontology

nodes.label: equivalent class
nodes.def: A logical axiom declaring two class expressions to denote the same set of entities in an ontology.

nodes.label: equivalent property
nodes.def: A logical axiom declaring two properties to have identical semantics and extensions in an ontology.

nodes.label: existential restriction
nodes.def: A class restriction requiring that instances have at least one value for a specified property from a specified class.

nodes.label: fact checking
nodes.def: task of verifying the truthfulness of factual claims using knowledge graphs as a source of verified knowledge

nodes.label: formal ontology
nodes.def: An explicit specification of a conceptualization using a formal logic, enabling computational reasoning about domain structure.

nodes.label: foundational ontology
nodes.def: A top-level ontology supplying core metaphysical categories and relations for building domain ontologies on top of.

nodes.label: functional property
nodes.def: A property axiom stating that each entity can have at most one distinct value for this property.

nodes.label: graph
nodes.def: An abstract mathematical structure composed of nodes (vertices) and edges (connections) underlying all knowledge graph representations.

nodes.label: graph database
nodes.def: database management system optimized for graph storage and traversal operations enabling efficient knowledge graph queries

nodes.label: graph embedding
nodes.def: A learned low-dimensional vector representation of graph elements preserving structural and semantic proximity information.

nodes.label: graph neural network
nodes.def: A neural architecture designed to operate directly on graph-structured data, learning representations for nodes and edges.

nodes.label: graph query language
nodes.def: language designed for expressing pattern matching and traversal operations over graph-structured knowledge

nodes.label: graph traversal
nodes.def: The algorithmic process of visiting nodes and edges in a knowledge graph following defined patterns or strategies.

nodes.label: hierarchy
nodes.def: A parent-child tree structure imposing ordering among entities, fundamental to class taxonomies and part-whole relations.

nodes.label: hybrid reasoning
nodes.def: A reasoning approach combining multiple inference techniques such as description logic reasoning with rule-based logic programming.

nodes.label: indexing
nodes.def: The creation of auxiliary data structures enabling fast retrieval of triples matching given patterns in a triple store.

nodes.label: individual
nodes.def: A concrete instance of a class in an ontology, representing a specific entity in the domain rather than a type.

nodes.label: inductive learning
nodes.def: A learning setting where the model generalizes to entirely unseen entities not present during training.

nodes.label: inference
nodes.def: The process of deriving new implicit knowledge from explicit statements using logical rules and reasoning mechanisms.

nodes.label: inference engine
nodes.def: reasoning system that derives new implicit knowledge from explicit facts using logical rules and ontology constraints

nodes.label: instance of
nodes.def: A membership relation connecting an individual entity to the class it belongs to.

nodes.label: inverse functional property
nodes.def: A property axiom stating that the inverse of a property is functional, enabling inference of identity from property values.

nodes.label: inverse property
nodes.def: A logical axiom declaring that two properties are the mutual converse of each other in a relationship pair.

nodes.label: iri
nodes.def: Internationalized Resource Identifier — the global identifier standard for resources in the semantic web, replacing the older URI spec.

nodes.label: irreflexive property
nodes.def: A property axiom stating that no entity can relate to itself via the specified property.

nodes.label: json ld
nodes.def: JSON for Linked Data — a JSON-based serialization for RDF designed for ease of use by web developers.

nodes.label: knowledge base
nodes.def: A persistent storage system for structured knowledge, combining a knowledge graph with an inference engine and query interface.

nodes.label: knowledge completion inference
nodes.def: specialized inference focused on predicting missing facts by reasoning over existing knowledge graph structure

nodes.label: knowledge curation
nodes.def: ongoing process of reviewing validating updating and correcting knowledge stored in the graph

nodes.label: knowledge embedding
nodes.def: A vector representation of entities and relations in a knowledge graph learned to satisfy relational constraints geometrically.

nodes.label: knowledge graph
nodes.def: A structured representation of knowledge as a graph of entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges), enabling semantic querying and inference over interconnected data.

nodes.label: knowledge graph augmentation
nodes.def: process of enhancing an existing knowledge graph with additional facts entities or relations from external sources

nodes.label: knowledge graph completion
nodes.def: The task of automatically inferring missing facts in a knowledge graph to improve its coverage and utility.

nodes.label: knowledge graph construction
nodes.def: end-to-end process of building a knowledge graph from raw data sources including extraction integration and curation

nodes.label: knowledge graph embedding
nodes.def: specific embedding technique that projects knowledge graph components into continuous vector representations

nodes.label: knowledge graph fusion
nodes.def: process of merging multiple knowledge graphs into a unified graph resolving conflicts and eliminating duplicates

nodes.label: knowledge graph indexing
nodes.def: creation of efficient data structures enabling fast lookup and retrieval of entities and relations in the graph

nodes.label: knowledge graph linking
nodes.def: establishment of cross-references between entities in different knowledge graphs forming a linked knowledge network

nodes.label: knowledge graph query optimization
nodes.def: techniques for efficiently executing complex queries over large-scale knowledge graphs using indexing and planning

nodes.label: knowledge graph revision
nodes.def: process of modifying the knowledge graph to correct errors incorporate new information or adapt to changing knowledge

nodes.label: knowledge graph schema learning
nodes.def: automatic discovery of structural patterns and typing schemas from entity relationships in the graph

nodes.label: knowledge graph storage
nodes.def: physical organization of knowledge graph data in storage systems including indexing partitioning and caching strategies

nodes.label: knowledge ontology matching
nodes.def: process of aligning entities and relations between a knowledge graph and an external ontology reference schema

nodes.label: knowledge representation
nodes.def: The field of study concerned with how to formally encode knowledge so that computer systems can reason about it.

nodes.label: link neighbor
nodes.def: An entity adjacent to a given entity via one or more edges in a knowledge graph, forming the local neighborhood context.

nodes.label: link prediction
nodes.def: The task of inferring missing or likely future relationships between entities in a knowledge graph.

nodes.label: linked data
nodes.def: A set of best practices for publishing and interlinking structured data on the web using RDF and HTTP IRIs.

nodes.label: literal
nodes.def: A raw data value (string, number, date) in an RDF triple, as opposed to a reference to another entity via IRI.

nodes.label: literal value
nodes.def: data value like string number date or boolean attached to entities as property objects in knowledge representation

nodes.label: materialization
nodes.def: The pre-computation and storage of all inferred facts derivable from explicit knowledge, trading space for query speed.

nodes.label: module extraction
nodes.def: The extraction of a minimal relevant subset of an ontology satisfying all axioms relevant to a given signature of interest.

nodes.label: multi hop reasoning
nodes.def: The ability to traverse and compose multiple relational steps in a knowledge graph to derive complex inferred conclusions.

nodes.label: n triples
nodes.def: A line-oriented RDF serialization format where each triple appears on a single line as subject predicate object separated by spaces.

nodes.label: named entity recognition
nodes.def: NLP task of locating and classifying named entities in text into predefined categories like person organization location

nodes.label: named graph
nodes.def: An RDF graph identified by an IRI, enabling provenance tracking, access control, and multi-context knowledge representation.

nodes.label: namespace
nodes.def: A logical grouping of related identifiers under a common prefix, disambiguating terms and providing context for schema definitions.

nodes.label: neural symbolic
nodes.def: An approach integrating neural network learning with symbolic reasoning for enhanced knowledge graph completion and inference.

nodes.label: object
nodes.def: The third element of an RDF triple — the value or entity that is the target of the predicate assertion.

nodes.label: object property
nodes.def: A property type in OWL whose value is another individual entity, expressing binary relations between resources.

nodes.label: ontology
nodes.def: A formal explicit specification of a shared conceptualization, defining concepts, categories, properties, and relations within a domain of discourse.

nodes.label: ontology alignment
nodes.def: The result of ontology matching — a set of mappings establishing equivalence, subsumption, or other relations between aligned entities.

nodes.label: ontology engineering
nodes.def: The discipline of building, maintaining, and evolving ontologies, encompassing methodology, tools, and best practices.

nodes.label: ontology evaluation
nodes.def: The systematic assessment of ontology quality along dimensions including correctness, completeness, and coherence.

nodes.label: ontology import
nodes.def: The mechanism in OWL for one ontology to formally incorporate the axioms and declarations from another referenced ontology.

nodes.label: ontology learning
nodes.def: The automated or semi-automated extraction of ontology components from data sources such as text or structured data.

nodes.label: ontology matching
nodes.def: The automated process of finding semantic correspondences between entities from different ontologies.

nodes.label: ontology merge
nodes.def: The process of combining two or more ontologies into a unified ontology based on established alignments.

nodes.label: ontology module
nodes.def: extractable self-contained subset of an ontology that preserves semantic consistency and can be shared independently

nodes.label: ontology pattern
nodes.def: reusable solution template for modeling common domain concepts like part-whole temporal events and qualifiers

nodes.label: context window
nodes.def: The finite token sequence an LLM can process in a single forward pass; defines the maximum input + output capacity bounded by architecture or inference config

nodes.label: context length
nodes.def: Total number of tokens (input + output) an LLM supports; the hard ceiling on how much text can be loaded into context_window at once

nodes.label: long term memory
nodes.def: Information persisted across sessions, tasks, or deployments; requires external storage and retrieval mechanisms since it cannot fit in context_window

nodes.label: working memory
nodes.def: The transient token budget allocated for active reasoning within a single model call; scratch space for chain_of_thought and intermediate results

nodes.label: attention mechanism
nodes.def: The core operation allowing each token to attend to all others; scaled dot-product attention is the standard. Memory and context are both outputs of attention computation.

nodes.label: vector database
nodes.def: Storage system indexing embeddings for similarity search; backbone of RAG. Examples: Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, FAISS. Enables retrieval from vast document collections.

nodes.label: conversation history
nodes.def: The chronological log of user_message and assistant_message turns in a session; the primary raw material for context_building

nodes.label: em event
nodes.def: A discrete unit of experience stored in episodic memory — a single interaction, task completion, or notable outcome.

nodes.label: effective context
nodes.def: Portion of context_window the model actually leverages for any given generation; often less than the full window due to attention patterns

nodes.label: retrieval augmented generation
nodes.def: Architecture pattern where an LLM queries external knowledge sources and injects results into context before generating a response; combines memory_retrieval with generation

nodes.label: sliding window
nodes.def: Fixed-size contiguous subset of recent tokens kept in working_memory as new tokens arrive and old ones are evicted

nodes.label: context compression
nodes.def: Transforming a large context into a shorter equivalent representation — via summarization, extraction, or lossy summarization — to fit within context_limit

nodes.label: attention sinks
nodes.def: Special tokens that accumulate disproportionate attention mass, enabling efficient long-context modeling without explicit positional encoding

nodes.label: chain of thought
nodes.def: Producing intermediate reasoning steps before final answer; when demonstrated in context, subsequent reasoning follows the pattern. A form of contextual procedural memory.

nodes.label: kv cache
nodes.def: The key-value tensors cached during transformer self-attention to avoid recomputing activations for previously-seen tokens

nodes.label: prompt engineering
nodes.def: Crafting input text to elicit desired outputs; includes instruction design, example selection, formatting, and context structuring.

nodes.label: chunking strategy
nodes.def: How documents are split into retrieval units; choices affect recall/precision: fixed-size, semantic (by sentences/paragraphs), recursive, or agentic splitting.

nodes.label: episodic memory

nodes.label: in context learning
nodes.def: Model adapts behavior based on examples provided in the context window; no weight updates. Related to memory since examples must fit in context.

nodes.label: memory retrieval
nodes.def: The act of fetching stored memory entries — by semantic similarity, keyword, metadata, or temporal proximity — to include in context

nodes.label: token boundary marker
nodes.def: The positional delimiter marking the transition from input context to output generation; tokens before this marker are provided context, tokens after are to be generated.

nodes.label: embedding model

nodes.label: kg entity
nodes.def: A node in the knowledge_graph representing a distinct thing — concrete object, person, event, or concept — identified by a unique identifier

nodes.def: The portion of context_length reserved for generated tokens; equals context_length minus input_token_budget minus overhead tokens.

nodes.label: overflow threshold
nodes.def: The position or token count at which the model behavior shifts from normal processing to truncation or error; often slightly below context_boundary.

nodes.def: Persistent preamble injected into every conversation turn; anchors persona, behavioral rules, and long_term_memory instructions

nodes.def: A graph-structured representation of entities and their relationships; used as a structured form of semantic_memory with traversable edges

nodes.label: maximum position

nodes.def: Encoding that injects positional information into token representations since attention is permutation-invariant. Choices: sinusoidal, RoPE, ALiBi. Affects how context scales.

nodes.label: scratchpad
nodes.def: Explicit intermediate reasoning space written by the model itself; a form of ephemeral working_memory externalized to tokens

nodes.label: semantic memory
nodes.def: Memory storing general world knowledge, facts, and concepts rather than specific personal experiences; queried via retrieval for grounding

nodes.label: semantic network
nodes.def: Graph of concepts connected by typed edges; models can store and traverse this structure for relational reasoning

nodes.label: semantic similarity
nodes.def: Measure of meaning overlap between two text fragments in embedding_space; the basis for associative_memory retrieval

nodes.label: sequence position
nodes.def: The ordinal index of a token within the full context sequence; constrained to be less than or equal to maximum_position.

nodes.def: The arithmetic difference between current position or token count and context_boundary; the remaining room before overflow_threshold is reached.

nodes.label: truncation strategy
nodes.def: Policy for removing old context when context_overflow occurs; options include FIFO, importance-weighted, and semantic summarization

nodes.label: active retrieval
nodes.def: Retrieval triggered during generation, not just at start; model decides when to query based on generated content. HyDE and self-RAG are examples.

nodes.label: adapters in context
nodes.def: Lightweight modules inserted in transformer layers trained on specific tasks; combined with context for efficient multi-task performance.

nodes.label: adaptive context
nodes.def: Dynamically adjusting context composition based on the current task, user query, or observed model behavior mid-conversation

nodes.label: agent memory
nodes.def: Structured memory holding an agent's beliefs, goals, preferences, and accumulated experience; feeds into context_building for downstream tasks

nodes.label: agentic rag
nodes.def: RAG where the LLM orchestrates multiple retrieval steps, decides what to query, and synthesizes from multiple sources. Reflection and planning loops.

nodes.label: alibi position embedding
nodes.def: Attention with Linear Biases — a position embedding scheme derived from attention scores, enabling better length extrapolation than absolute positions

nodes.label: ann index
nodes.def: The data structure or index built to support approximate_nearest_neighbors queries over a vector collection

nodes.label: associative retrieval
nodes.def: Retrieving memories by content similarity rather than exact match; enabled by embedding space proximity.

nodes.label: attention as memory
nodes.def: Perspective that attention mechanism itself is a form of memory retrieval; queries search keys to retrieve values, analogous to content-addressable memory.

nodes.def: The hard edge position within context where context_overflow triggers if exceeded; exactly context_length minus one for the output region.

nodes.def: Farthest retrievable or presentable token distance from current position; the effective reach of memory_access

nodes.def: The multiplier relating raw context_length to effective_context; models with improved attention patterns achieve factors closer to one.

nodes.def: Ordering structure by event importance or impact; enables retrieval by significance rather than recency.

nodes.label: em temporal index
nodes.def: Organizational structure mapping events to time ranges; enables retrieval by temporal proximity.

nodes.label: embedding dimensionality
nodes.def: Number of dimensions in the embedding_space; higher captures more nuance but increases storage and retrieval_cost

nodes.label: hierarchical chunking

nodes.def: An attribute attached to a kg_entity describing a feature or quality; differs from kg_relationship in that it terminates in a literal value rather than another entity

nodes.label: kg relationship
nodes.def: A typed directed edge connecting a source kg_entity to a target kg_entity; the edge carries a predicate label defining the relation semantics

nodes.def: The atomic unit of a knowledge_graph: a (subject kg_entity, predicate label, object kg_entity) tuple; equivalently a single kg_relationship with its endpoints

nodes.label: memory efficiency
nodes.def: Ratio of useful information retained per unit of memory storage or context_token budget

nodes.label: memory persistence
nodes.def: How long memory survives; session memory (within conversation), user memory (across sessions), or permanent memory (until explicitly deleted).

nodes.label: memory window
nodes.def: The subset of episodic_memory available for retrieval at any time; analogous to context_window but for long_term_storage

nodes.label: overlapping chunks
nodes.def: Chunking strategy where adjacent chunks share boundary tokens to prevent information loss at chunk_boundaries

nodes.label: position index

nodes.def: The ratio of semantic content units per token for a given text under a particular tokenization_scheme; affects how much text fits within context_length.

nodes.label: tokenization scheme
nodes.def: The specific algorithm determining how raw text is segmented into discrete tokens; determines token_boundary_marker positions and token_density for any given text.

nodes.label: approximate nearest neighbors
nodes.def: Algorithms that trade exactness for speed in vector_search, enabling sub-linear retrieval over large embedding indices

nodes.label: associative memory
nodes.def: Recall triggered by related concepts; attention mechanism is a form of content-addressable associative memory enabling retrieval by similarity.

nodes.label: attention overhead
nodes.def: Computational overhead of attention mechanisms relative to other operations; dominates total compute for long contexts.

nodes.label: attention sink token position
nodes.def: Fixed or learned position indices within context_length that accumulate disproportionate attention mass

nodes.label: attribution
nodes.def: Tracing model outputs back to source context tokens or retrieved memories; essential for factual grounding and verification

nodes.label: c util 003
nodes.def: Task performance variance: measurable change in downstream task accuracy when the same information is repositioned within context_window; reveals position-dependent bias in effecti

nodes.label: context caching
nodes.def: Storing computed key-value pairs from prior forward passes to avoid recomputation on repeated or overlapping context prefixes

nodes.label: context grounding
nodes.def: Ensuring generation is anchored in the provided context rather than ungrounded model knowledge; key for retrieval_augmented_generation quality

nodes.label: context summarization
nodes.def: Replacing a long context segment with a distilled summary that preserves key semantics while consuming fewer tokens

nodes.label: context utilization

nodes.label: conversational context
nodes.def: The aggregate of discourse_memory, entity_tracking, and conversation_history that defines the current interaction state

nodes.label: coreference resolution

nodes.label: cosine similarity

nodes.label: discourse memory
nodes.def: High-level structure of conversation: goals, commitments, questions raised; persists beyond individual turn context

nodes.label: em context bundle
nodes.def: The surrounding context of an event including user inputs, system responses, and environmental state at the time.

nodes.label: em episode marker

nodes.label: em interaction record
nodes.def: Structured log of the exchange pairs (prompt/response) comprising an event.

nodes.label: em outcome
nodes.def: The result or consequence of an event — success, failure, or partial completion — recorded for outcome-based retrieval.

nodes.label: em state snapshot
nodes.def: Captured system state (context window contents, active variables, user profile) at the moment of an event.

nodes.label: em timestamp
nodes.def: Temporal marker indicating when an event occurred; enables chronological ordering of episodic entries.

nodes.label: token endpoint

nodes.label: id token

nodes.label: refresh token

nodes.label: acr claim

nodes.label: authorization server
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 server that authenticates the resource owner, obtains consent, and issues access tokens and optionally refresh tokens and ID tokens.

nodes.label: bearer token
nodes.def: Token type defined in RFC 6750; any party possessing the token may use it; security relies on transport TLS and token secrecy.

nodes.label: claims policy enforcement

nodes.label: expires in
nodes.def: Integer seconds indicating access token lifetime; returned alongside access_token in token response.

nodes.label: introspection endpoint
nodes.def: RFC 7662 endpoint allowing resource servers to validate access tokens; returns active status, scope, expiry, and other token metadata.

nodes.label: access token introspection

nodes.label: acr

nodes.label: acr requirement

nodes.label: acr values

nodes.label: authorization endpoint
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 endpoint where the resource owner authenticates and grants consent; returns authorization_code via redirect or form_post response.

nodes.label: claims verification
nodes.def: Relying party validation that returned claims match what was requested in the claims_parameter, checking essential claims are present and values satisfy policy constraints.

nodes.label: essential claim directive
nodes.def: Claim marked as required by the relying party; identity provider must return this claim or return an error satisfying the acr_values if unable to fulfill.

nodes.label: grant type
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 parameter identifying which authorization flow is being used; values: authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, password (deprecated).

nodes.label: identity provider
nodes.def: OIDC term for the authorization server that also acts as the authentication authority; issues id_token and exposes userinfo.

nodes.label: partial claims fulfillment
nodes.def: Server response state where only a subset of requested claims are returned; occurs when policy or consent excludes some claims from the request.

nodes.label: relying party
nodes.def: OIDC term for the client application that relies on the identity provider's id_token for user authentication.

nodes.label: resource indicator
nodes.def: RFC 8707 parameter specifying the target resource server URI; server issues access token scoped to that specific resource, not just the general API.

nodes.label: state

nodes.label: token introspection
nodes.def: RFC 7662 introspection: protected endpoint where resource servers POST access_token to get its status, scope, expiration, and active flag.

nodes.label: userinfo endpoint
nodes.def: OIDC protected endpoint returning user claims as a JSON object; called with access_token after successful authentication; claims may overlap with id_token.

nodes.label: access denied

nodes.label: access token audience restricted

nodes.label: access token format type

nodes.label: access token hash
nodes.def: OIDC id_token at_hash claim computed as base64url(left-half(SHA256(access_token))); RP verifies to confirm access_token was not tampered with.

nodes.label: access token presented to
nodes.def: The resource_server that receives and validates the access_token on each protected API call; the token is forwarded via HTTP Authorization header using the bearer scheme.

nodes.label: access token scope

nodes.label: account selection required
nodes.def: OIDC error when prompt=select_account but the user has multiple accounts and must pick one.

nodes.label: achieved acr
nodes.def: The authentication context class reference actually satisfied by the OpenID Provider during an authentication event; carried in the id_token acr claim; may differ from requested_ac

nodes.label: acr claim value
nodes.def: The specific ACC URI returned in the acr claim of id_token, must be one of or satisfy the requested acr_values.

nodes.label: acr class reference
nodes.def: The URI string value that uniquely identifies a specific authentication context class; the atomic element within acr_values; examples drawn from SAML ACR URN namespace.

nodes.label: acr essential
nodes.def: OIDC parameter flag accompanying acr_values indicating whether the requested ACR is required (essential=true) or preferred; when essential=true and no acceptable ACR can be satisfi

nodes.def: The 'acr' claim embedded in the signed id_token; carries the achieved_acr identifier as a URI string; RP inspects this to verify authentication context requirements were met.

nodes.def: Identity provider condition when no requested ACC in acr_values can be satisfied, causing authentication failure per prompt=none semantics.

nodes.def: The algorithmic step the OP performs upon receiving acr_values: iterate the ordered list, evaluate each acr_class against the authentication that will be performed, return the firs

nodes.label: acr satisfaction
nodes.def: The OP evaluating its authentication mechanisms against the requested ACRs and determining which ones it can satisfy

nodes.label: authentication context class
nodes.def: A named authentication context class identified by a URI string; represents a defined level of assurance or authentication method category that an Identity Provider can declare it

nodes.label: authorization code
nodes.def: Short-lived credential exchanged for tokens at the token endpoint; exists to keep tokens out of the user-agent (browser) history and address bar.

nodes.label: authorization code flow
nodes.def: Primary OAuth 2.0 flow for web apps with a server-side component; uses authorization_endpoint then token_endpoint with the returned code.

nodes.label: authorization server metadata
nodes.def: RFC 8414 metadata document at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; lists server capabilities, endpoint URLs, grant types, and supported features.

nodes.label: ciba
nodes.def: RFC 9002 Client Initiated Backchannel Authentication; user initiates auth from a device, push notification is sent to their phone, RP polls for result.

nodes.label: client
nodes.def: Application making protected resource requests on behalf of the resource owner; classified as confidential (can hold secrets) or public (cannot).

nodes.label: client credentials grant
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 flow where the client authenticates with its own credentials and receives an access token representing the client itself (no user).

nodes.label: client id
nodes.def: Public identifier assigned by the authorization server to a client; used to identify which application is requesting authorization.

nodes.label: client secret
nodes.def: Confidential credential held by the client; used with authorization_code or client_credentials flows to authenticate the client to the token endpoint.

nodes.label: device flow
nodes.def: RFC 8628 OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant; user enters a code on a separate device while the client polls for authorization completion.

nodes.label: discovery document
nodes.def: Well-known URL pattern (RFC 5785) at /.well-known/openid-configuration exposing OIDC provider configuration JSON.

nodes.label: dpop proof
nodes.def: RFC 9449 Demonstrated Proof-of-Possession; client signs a JWT with its private key and includes DPoP header in token requests to bind the token to the key.

nodes.label: id token claim target
nodes.def: Claims section of claims_request specifying which claims the relying party wants embedded directly in the signed id_token JWT.

nodes.label: id token hint
nodes.def: OIDC parameter carrying a previously issued id_token; OP uses it to infer the user and potentially skip re-authentication or pre-fill consent.

nodes.label: invalid grant
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 error code when the provided authorization grant or refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked, or already used.

nodes.label: issuer
nodes.def: String identifier (typically URL) in id_token and access_token; relying parties validate tokens were issued by a trusted, matching issuer.

nodes.label: jwks uri
nodes.def: URL in discovery document pointing to JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) containing public keys used to verify id_token and access_token signatures.

nodes.label: login hint
nodes.def: OIDC parameter suggesting which account the user should log in with; may be email, username, or account selector hint.

nodes.label: max age
nodes.def: OIDC parameter specifying maximum seconds since last authentication; if elapsed, OP must re-authenticate before issuing id_token.

nodes.label: openid configuration
nodes.def: Discovery document served at /.well-known/openid-configuration; machine-readable metadata listing endpoints, supported features, and server capabilities.

nodes.label: pairwise identifiers
nodes.def: OIDC subject identifier strategy where each RP receives a different sub for the same user, preventing cross-RP user correlation.

nodes.label: pkce
nodes.def: RFC 7636 Proof Key for Code Exchange; mitigates authorization code interception by requiring code_verifier and code_challenge from the client.

nodes.label: prompt parameter
nodes.def: OIDC parameter controlling user interaction: none (no prompt, error if needed), login (force re-auth), consent (show approval screen), select_account.

nodes.label: pushed authorization request
nodes.def: RFC 9126 PAR: client POSTs authorization request parameters to par_endpoint first, receives request_uri for use at authorization_endpoint.

nodes.label: redirect uri
nodes.def: Callback URL the authorization server redirects to after consent; must be pre-registered with the authorization server and must match exactly.

nodes.label: resource owner
nodes.def: Entity capable of granting access to a protected resource; typically the end-user who authenticates to authorize the client's request.

nodes.label: revocation endpoint
nodes.def: RFC 7009 endpoint allowing clients to invalidate refresh or access tokens; supports bearer tokens and is advisory (server may retain copy).

nodes.label: scope
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 mechanism for requesting specific permission sets; space-delimited string (e.g. 'openid profile email'); server grants subset based on policy.

nodes.label: subject identifier
nodes.def: The 'sub' claim in id_token: a unique stable identifier assigned by the identity provider to the user; pairwise vs public based on RP.

nodes.label: token exchange

nodes.label: token type
nodes.def: OAuth 2.0 parameter indicating how the access_token is to be presented to the resource server, typically Bearer, specifying the authorization scheme to use in requests.

nodes.label: ui locales
nodes.def: OIDC parameter indicating user's preferred languages for the consent/userinfo UI; BCP 47 language tag list.

nodes.label: user claims consent
nodes.def: End-user authorization for the identity provider to release specific claims; may be granted, denied, or limited compared to what relying party requested.

nodes.label: userinfo claim target
nodes.def: Claims section of claims_request specifying which claims the relying party wants returned from the userinfo_endpoint after token exchange.

nodes.label: voluntary claim directive
nodes.def: Claim requested by the relying party but not mandated; identity provider may omit based on policy, user consent, or availability without error.

nodes.label: acr request
nodes.def: The subset of an OIDC Authorization Request that specifies acr_values (and optionally acr_values essential flag); the structured representation of the RP's authentication context r

nodes.label: acr satisfaction policy

nodes.label: authentication level
nodes.def: Level of Assurance semantics governing the ordering of ACC URIs in acr_values; higher-positioned ACCs imply stronger authentication requirements.

nodes.label: authentication method reference
nodes.def: The AMR claim in id_token listing specific authentication methods used (e.g. OTP, swk); distinct from acr which addresses context class; both may coexist in id_token to fully chara

nodes.label: authorization code interception
nodes.def: Threat where malware or network attacker steals the authorization code from the browser redirect; mitigated by PKCE requiring proof at token time.

nodes.label: authz code

nodes.def: OIDC Logout spec using direct server-to-server POST to RP logout endpoint; more reliable than front-channel but requires RP endpoint.

nodes.label: bearer token scheme
